adapterChannel.label: Adapter version
adapterChannel.description: Install and Upgrade use the version codeg has reviewed and pinned. Latest switches them to the package's newest npm release at that moment; if installing it fails, codeg falls back to the pinned version and notes it in the install log.
adapterChannel.latestWarning: Newest releases are unreviewed and can break this agent in codeg, and occasionally a release is known broken. Version Status shows what is actually installed.

hostTools.label: Let the agent handle files and commands
hostTools.description: codeg stops serving file access and terminal commands, so the agent runs them in its own process — where its own sandbox and permission rules apply. Delegating to other agents is also turned off, since that would route the same work back through codeg. codeg adds no sandbox itself, so turn this on only if the agent has one configured.

AcpAgentSettings.modelHintDefault: Leave empty to use system default model.
AcpAgentSettings.generalConfigDescriptionClaude: Supports quick configuration for API URL, API Key and Claude models, and syncs with native JSON config.

multiAgent.description: Allow active agents to delegate sub-tasks to other agents.
multiAgent.enableHint: When off, the delegate_to_agent tool is hidden from the agent's MCP catalog.
multiAgent.withheldByHostTools: {agents} will not get the delegation tools: their per-agent “Let the agent handle files and commands” switch is on.
multiAgent.depthHint: Allowed range: {min}–{max}. Caps how deep a chain (root → child → grandchild …) can recurse.
multiAgent.completedCacheHint: In-memory cache of finished sub-agent results, held only while the delegating session is running and cleared automatically when it ends. Over this budget the oldest results are dropped from memory first (still viewable in the sub-agent's own session); 0 = unlimited (still cleared when the session ends).

grok.configDescription: Configure Grok here. The controls below — permission mode, reasoning effort, an optional custom (BYO endpoint) model, and compaction — merge into ~/.grok/config.toml, preserving your other keys and comments. Sign-in uses your XAI_API_KEY or `grok login`. Other keys stay editable under Advanced.
grok.authModeApiKeyHint: Authenticate with an XAI_API_KEY from the xAI console — for non-interactive or headless runs. Stored in this agent's environment.
grok.authModeCustomHint: Use a bring-your-own endpoint: define a custom model below with its own base URL and API key. It becomes Grok's default model.
grok.subscriptionHint: Sign in with `grok login` (SuperGrok / X Premium+). No API key is stored.
grok.loginHint: Run this in a terminal to sign in, then reopen these settings:
grok.configTomlHint: Saved verbatim as the whole ~/.grok/config.toml. Invalid TOML is rejected so a typo never truncates your file.
grok.configTomlPlaceholder:
# Keys other than the controls above, e.g.
# [mcp_servers.*], [cli], [permission] rules.
grok.customModelHint: Point Grok at a custom or self-hosted endpoint. codeg writes a per-model `[model.*]` block and makes it the default. Leave the Model ID empty to remove it.
grok.customModelIdHint: Registered as a `[model.*]` block and sent to the API as the model name; also set as `[models].default`.
grok.customApiKeyHint: Stored inline in `[model.*].api_key`, scoped to this endpoint.
grok.customContextWindowHint: Optional. Drives auto-compact timing; leave empty for the endpoint default.
grok.autoCompactHint: Compact the conversation when context usage reaches this percent (Grok default 85). Written to `[session]`.

cursor.configDescription: Configure Cursor here. Choose an authentication method — official subscription (browser sign-in) or a Cursor API key for headless/server machines — then pick a model and edit the CLI's permission rules and sandbox. codeg writes them into ~/.cursor/cli-config.json, shared with the cursor-agent CLI.
cursor.authUnverifiedHint: cursor-agent still has a login stored, but it could not be used against Cursor just now — usually an expired session. Sessions will fail with "Authentication required" until you sign in again; the CLI has no way to refresh a browser login on its own.
cursor.authUnverifiedHintApiKey: cursor-agent has an API key stored, but Cursor rejected it just now — usually a revoked, expired, or mistyped key. Sessions will fail with "Authentication required" until you save a working key below.
cursor.loginHint: Run this in a terminal to sign in with your Cursor account (a browser window opens), then hit refresh:
cursor.loginHintRemote: Run this on the codeg host where cursor-agent is installed, not on this machine, then hit refresh. That host usually has no browser to open, so run it with NO_OPEN_BROWSER=1 — it prints a sign-in URL for you to open in your own browser instead. For an unattended server, switch the method above to API key.
cursor.apiKeyHint: CURSOR_API_KEY — a Cursor Dashboard account key, an alternative to browser login for headless/server machines. Not a third-party or OpenAI key.
cursor.modelHint: Passed to the CLI as --model at session start. Leave on default to let Cursor choose.
cursor.modelVariantHint: Cursor ships every combination as its own model id; these controls pick the right one. They set the launch default — a session can change model, thinking and Fast at any time from the composer.
cursor.permissionsDescription: Visual editor for the CLI's permission rules (cli-config.json). Allow rules run without prompting; deny rules are always blocked.
cursor.permissionModeHint: Run Everything launches sessions with --force: every tool call is auto-allowed except deny rules, with no confirmation prompts (an organization policy may downgrade it to allow-rule matching). Takes effect for new sessions.
cursor.permissionModeAskHint: Ask before running sends each tool call to you for approval, with Cursor's own "Allow always" option — choosing it appends a rule to the Allowed list below, so the same call runs unprompted next time.
cursor.rulesSyntaxHint: Rule syntax: Shell(cmd), Read(path/glob), Write(path/glob), WebFetch(domain), Mcp(server:tool) — deny rules always win.
cursor.advancedHint: The whole ~/.cursor/cli-config.json. Saving writes the file verbatim — the structured controls above merge into it instead.
cursor.subscriptionHint: Sign in with your Cursor account and use Cursor's models.
cursor.customApiKeyRequired: A Cursor API key is required.
cursor.authModeApiKeyHint: Authenticate with a Cursor account API key from the Cursor dashboard — for headless or server machines. This is a Cursor account key, not a third-party/OpenAI endpoint: cursor-agent only talks to Cursor's own backend. To use a codex/OpenAI-compatible endpoint, use the Codex agent instead.
cursor.modelsNeedAuth: Sign in to load the model list.

qoder.configDescription: Sign in to Qoder here. Everything else the CLI reads lives in one file — $QODER_CONFIG_DIR/settings.json (default ~/.qoder), shared with the qoder CLI — and is edited raw below. Model and reasoning effort are not here: Qoder reports them over ACP, so the composer's own selectors own them per session.
qoder.loginHint: Run this in a terminal to sign in with your Qoder account (a browser window opens), then hit refresh:
qoder.tokenHint: QODER_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN — a non-interactive credential for machines where the browser sign-in can't run. Leave empty to use the qoder account login.
qoder.advancedHint: The whole settings.json, written verbatim on save — which is also the only way to delete a key.

antigravity.configDescription: Antigravity needs an authentication method before it can start a session. The choice is written to auth.type in $GEMINI_HOME/antigravity-acp/settings.json, which is the only place the ACP server looks — without it every new session fails with "Authentication required". Model and session mode are not here: Antigravity reports them over ACP, so the composer's own selectors own them per session.

methodHints.oauth-personal: Your Google account, on any Antigravity plan including the free tier. The first new session opens a browser to finish signing in; the token is then cached and reused. No browser on this machine? Use the browser-free sign-in below.
methodHints.oauth-business: Your Gemini Enterprise account. Needs a GCP project and location, and the first new session opens a browser. No browser on this machine? Use the browser-free sign-in below.
methodHints.gemini-api-key: A key for the Gemini Developer API, passed to the agent as GEMINI_API_KEY.
methodHints.agent-platform: Formerly Vertex AI. Use an API key, or a project and location with Application Default Credentials (gcloud auth application-default login).

antigravity.googleApiKeyHint: Optional. When set it is used on its own — the project and location below are ignored. Leave it empty to authenticate with Application Default Credentials instead.
antigravity.missingGeminiApiKey: Enter a Gemini API key, or pick a different authentication method — sessions will fail to start without it.
antigravity.missingAgentPlatformConfig: Enter an API key, or both a project and a location — sessions will fail to start without one of the two.
antigravity.missingEnterpriseConfig: Gemini Enterprise needs both a project and a location.
antigravity.settingsFileHint: Saved to auth.type in this file. Any other keys you put there are preserved.
antigravity.syncSkipped: Your choice was saved, but codeg could not write it to the ACP server's settings.json, so Antigravity will keep authenticating the way that file says. Set auth.type in it yourself, or move it aside and save again.

headless.title: Sign in without a browser on this machine
headless.description: Antigravity runs the Google sign-in itself, on the machine the agent runs on. When there is no browser there — codeg on a server with no desktop — the first session waits five minutes and then fails. Start the sign-in here instead: open the link on any device, then paste back the address you land on.
headless.saveFirst: Save first — the sign-in uses the stored settings, not what is typed above.
headless.step1: 1. Open this link and sign in to Google.
headless.step2: 2. Your browser will end up on {redirectUri} and fail to connect — that is expected. Copy that whole address out of the address bar and paste it here.
headless.signedIn: Signed in. New sessions will use this account.
headless.alreadySignedIn: Antigravity already had a valid token, so it signed in without a link.
headless.credentialHint: The token is cached here. Copy this file to another machine with no desktop to sign that one in too.

signOut.title: Signed in as the wrong account?
signOut.description: Antigravity caches the Google account it signed in as and reuses it silently, so signing in again cannot reach a different one. Signing out discards the stored credential; any running Antigravity sessions end first, because they would otherwise write the old account back.
signOut.done: Signed out. Sign in again to pick a different account.

antigravity.tempReclaimHint: Older versions of codeg could not clean up the temporary directory this agent unpacks on every launch. This scans the system temp folder for those leftovers. That folder is shared with other applications, so nothing is deleted until you confirm, and anything still in use is skipped.
antigravity.tempReclaimSkipped: {count} skipped (still in use or too recent).
antigravity.tempReclaimConfirmBody: This permanently deletes {size}. The system temp folder is shared with other applications, so check each path before confirming — anything still in use is skipped.

deepseek.baseUrlHint: Leave empty for the official endpoint. Applies to sessions started after the save — reconnect a running session to pick it up.
deepseek.baseUrlInvalid: Enter a full http(s) URL with no query string, for example https://api.deepseek.com
deepseek.apiKeyHint: Passed to the agent as DEEPSEEK_API_KEY. An environment variable outranks the credentials file, so leave this empty if you sign in through the terminal.

codex.configDescription: Supports quick configuration for API URL, API Key and model name, and syncs with `auth.json` / `config.toml`.
codex.chatgptSubscriptionHint: Log in with ChatGPT official subscription, no API Key required
codex.apiKeyHint: Connect using API Key to OpenAI or compatible API services
codex.enableDefaultModeRequestUserInputAria: Allow Codex to ask questions in Default mode
codex.enableDefaultModeRequestUserInputHint: Codex may only call its request_user_input tool in Plan mode. Turn this on to let it ask you questions in ordinary turns too. Writes [features].default_mode_request_user_input to ~/.codex/config.toml; the flag is still under development upstream. Takes effect on the next session.
codex.enableFastAria: Enable Fast service tier for Codex
codex.sandboxGroupHint: Written to the global ~/.codex/config.toml, so codex CLI and IDE sessions see it too. These are thread defaults: they govern the turns codex starts on its own (/goal, /review, /compact). Ordinary prompts use the composer's approval preset instead. Restart a session to pick up changes.
codex.sandboxShadowedWarning: config.toml sets default_permissions, so codex resolves permissions through that profile and ignores sandbox_mode entirely. Remove default_permissions to use the controls below.
codex.sandboxPermissionsTableWarning: config.toml defines [permissions] profiles but no default_permissions, which makes codex refuse to start. Set one in the raw editor below.
codex.approvalPolicy_on-request: On request — the model decides when to ask

permissions.description: Decide which actions run on their own, prompt you first, or are blocked. Written to the permission block of opencode.json and applied once you save below.

permissions.invalidBlock: The permission block has a shape codeg does not recognize. Edit it in the native JSON below, or use Reset to start over.
permissions.orderingUnsafe: A wildcard rule is written after specific tools, so OpenCode applies it to them as well — the rows below are not what is in force. Fix order moves every wildcard back to the front of its scope without changing a single value.
permissions.orderingUnsafeManual: One rule is shadowed by a later, more general pattern, so OpenCode never applies it — the rows below are not what is in force. Two overlapping patterns have no single right order; reorder them in the native JSON so the general one comes first.
permissions.agentOverrides: These agents override permissions and are applied last, so they win over everything here: {agents}. Edit them in the native JSON below, or turn on auto-accept to clear them.
permissions.legacyTools: The legacy top-level tools map denies a tool. OpenCode folds it into the permissions, so it applies on top of everything shown here. Edit it in the native JSON below, or turn on auto-accept to clear it.
permissions.autoAcceptHint: Every tool call — shell commands, file edits, paths outside the project — runs without asking. Turning this on replaces the per-tool settings below with a single allow-all rule, and clears the per-agent permission overrides and legacy tool toggles that would otherwise still block.
permissions.globalHint: The * rule: what applies to anything the tools below do not override.
permissions.rulesHint: Matched against the tool input, last match wins — so put the broad patterns first. * matches any characters, ? matches exactly one, and a leading ~ expands to your home directory.

tips.tileTabs: Right-click any conversation tab and choose Tile Display to see multiple sessions side by side.
tips.pinTab: Double-click a conversation tab to pin it, so a newly opened session won't auto-replace it.
tips.shortcutsNewSearch: <shortcut>{newConversation}</shortcut> opens a new conversation, <shortcut>{searchConversations}</shortcut> searches your history.
tips.slashAtMention: Type / in the input to trigger slash commands, or @ to reference a file from the project.
tips.pasteDropFiles: Paste a screenshot or drop a file directly onto the input to attach it.
tips.queueMessage: While the agent is replying, keep typing — your next message gets queued and auto-sent when it finishes.
tips.draftAutoSave: Unsent drafts are auto-saved per conversation and restored when you come back.
tips.forkFromTurn: Any completed reply has Fork from here — branch the conversation at that message into a new tab.
tips.exportConversation: Right-click inside the conversation to export it as Markdown, HTML, or an image.
tips.chatChannels: Connect Telegram / Lark / WeChat under Settings → Chat Channels to continue from your phone.
tips.shortcutsAuxPanel: <shortcut>{toggleAuxPanel}</shortcut> toggles the right panel to view this session's touched files and Git changes.
tips.shortcutsTerminalSidebar: <shortcut>{toggleTerminal}</shortcut> opens the built-in terminal, <shortcut>{toggleSidebar}</shortcut> toggles the sidebar.
tips.customShortcuts: Every shortcut is fully remappable under Settings → Shortcuts.
tips.webService: Enable Settings → Web Service so teammates can reach the same codeg from a browser.
tips.fusionMode: Open a file or diff to automatically show it alongside the conversation.
tips.quickMessages: Open the + button next to the input and pick Quick Messages to insert a saved snippet (manage them under Settings → Quick Messages).
tips.experts: The + button has an Expert Skills menu — preload roles like Debug or Planning with one click.
tips.taskBoard: To-dos run a task end to end — the agent works in its own worktree, then you review the diff and merge.
tips.automations: Automations run a saved prompt on a schedule — a nightly review, a recurring report — and each run can get its own worktree.
tips.tokenUsage: Click the conversation count in the status bar to open Token Usage — spend broken down by day, agent, model, and folder.
tips.mentionTargets: @ pulls in more than files — mention another agent to hand off a subtask, or reference a past session, a commit, or a skill.
tips.splitGroups: Right-click a tab and pick Split Right or Split Down to keep two conversations open in their own panes.
tips.worktrees: Open the branch button and pick New worktree so several agents can work the same repo without overwriting each other's files.
tips.importSessions: Already ran sessions in the terminal? A folder's menu has Import local sessions — bring that history into codeg.
tips.subSessions: When an agent delegates, the sub-session appears nested under it in the sidebar — expand the row to follow what each one did.
tips.liveFeedback: Live feedback in the + menu drops a note into the turn the agent is already running, without interrupting it.
tips.skillPacks: Settings → Skill Packs bundles coding experts, scientific research, and office skills — switch them on per agent.
tips.modelProviders: Settings → Model Providers takes your own API key or endpoint, and you pick the model right in the composer.
tips.workspaceBackground: Settings → Appearance sets a workspace background image, panel opacity, and the app's fonts.

AgentToolsSettings.title: In-conversation tools
AgentToolsSettings.description: Extra tools codeg gives an agent inside a conversation. Each is injected when the agent starts, so a change applies to agents started afterwards.

delegation.label: Delegation
delegation.short: Hand a task to another agent.
delegation.hint: Lets an agent hand a self-contained sub-task to another agent, which runs in its own session and reports back. The rest of it — how deep delegations may nest, which agent runs them — is the section just above.

feedback.label: Live Feedback
feedback.hint: Send notes and corrections to an agent while it's working. When the agent supports instant steering, your note is inserted into the running turn immediately; otherwise the agent gets a tool to check for your feedback — those agents typically only check when you mention it in your prompt, for example add "check my live feedback regularly" to your message.

ask.label: Ask user question
ask.short: Let the agent ask you before it decides.
ask.hint: Let agents pause and ask you a multiple-choice question that appears above the conversation input box. The agent waits until you answer (or skip).

sessions.label: Get session info
sessions.short: Look up past sessions and their results.
sessions.hint: Let agents look up a session you reference in your message (a session badge) to read its title, agent, status, workspace, token usage, and recent messages.

browser.label: Read and drive the built-in browser
browser.short: Open, read and act on pages in the built-in browser.
browser.hint: Lets an agent see which pages are open in the built-in browser, read the ones you share, and click and type on the ones you allow actions on. It can also open an address itself, point a tab somewhere else and close tabs. Off by default. Which page it may read is still yours to decide in that tab's toolbar — but note that with a standing sharing level set, a page the agent opens for itself is shared with it the moment that page loads. Turning this off takes effect at once, on agents already running too.

browserEval.label: Run code in the built-in browser
browserEval.short: Run its own code on a page you shared — without asking, unless you ask it to.
browserEval.hint: Let agents run their own JavaScript on a page you’ve shared. Off by default, and needs the switch above. Turning it on means snippets run without asking, so this switch is where the decision is made; Settings → Built-in browser can put each snippet in front of you instead.

automations.label: Create automations
automations.hint: Save the conversation as an automation that runs on a schedule. Off by default — it goes on to start agents on its own.

taskboard.label: Create to-do tasks
taskboard.hint: Queue a card on the to-do board from the conversation. Off by default — it writes app state.
